question: Deficiency of which vitamin causes the disease 'Beriberi', characterized by weakness, nerve damage and cardiovascular problems?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vitamin B1 (Thiamine).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Deficiency of Vitamin B1 (Thiamine) causes Beriberi, a disease affecting the nervous and cardiovascular systems, marked by muscle weakness, nerve damage and, in severe cases, heart failure. (थायमिन की कमी — बेरी-बेरी रोग)

 

• Beriberi has two main forms: 'dry' beriberi, which primarily affects the nervous system, and 'wet' beriberi, which primarily affects the cardiovascular system.

 

• The Dutch physician Christiaan Eijkman established the link between a diet of polished rice (lacking thiamine-rich husk) and beriberi, work for which he shared the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in 1929.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other vitamin-deficiency diseases: Vitamin C deficiency causes scurvy; Vitamin D deficiency causes rickets (in children) and osteomalacia (in adults); Vitamin A deficiency causes night blindness.

 

NOTE

 

• Vitamin B2/Riboflavin (Option 2): Deficiency causes Ariboflavinosis, marked by cracked lips and skin lesions.

 

• Vitamin B3/Niacin (Option 3): Deficiency causes Pellagra, characterised by dermatitis, diarrhoea and dementia.

 

• Vitamin B12/Cobalamin (Option 4): Deficiency causes pernicious (megaloblastic) anaemia.

question: The 'Border-Gavaskar Trophy' is contested in Test cricket series between which two countries?
solution_text:
The correct answer is India and Australia.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Border-Gavaskar Trophy is awarded to the winner of Test cricket series played between India and Australia, instituted in 1996. (बॉर्डर-गावस्कर ट्रॉफी — भारत-ऑस्ट्रेलिया)

 

• It is named after two legendary former captains and batters: Allan Border of Australia and Sunil Gavaskar of India.

 

• As of the 2023 series, India held the trophy continuously since 2017, having won or retained it in multiple series against Australia.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• India and Australia also contest limited-overs cricket, though the Border-Gavaskar Trophy specifically refers to their Test series.

 

NOTE

 

• India and England (Option 1): Contest the Pataudi Trophy, renamed in 2007 (from the earlier Freedom Trophy) in honour of the father-son Nawabs of Pataudi who captained both countries.

 

• India and South Africa (Option 2): Contest the Freedom Trophy, commemorating the freedom struggles of both nations.

 

• India and New Zealand (Option 4): Their bilateral Test series does not have a dedicated named trophy.

question: The anti-defection law, which provides for the disqualification of members of Parliament or State Legislatures on grounds of defection, is contained in which Schedule of the Indian Constitution?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tenth Schedule.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The anti-defection law is contained in the Tenth Schedule of the Constitution, inserted by the 52nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1985. (दलबदल विरोधी कानून — दसवीं अनुसूची)

 

• It lays down the grounds on which elected members of Parliament and State Legislatures can be disqualified for defection from their political party.

 

• Decisions on disqualification under the Tenth Schedule are made by the Speaker/Chairman of the House concerned, and this decision is subject to judicial review, as held by the Supreme Court in Kihoto Hollohan v. Zachillhu (1992).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 91st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003 further strengthened the anti-defection law by removing the earlier exception that allowed a one-third split of a party to escape disqualification, permitting only a two-thirds merger.

 

NOTE

 

• Eighth Schedule (Option 1): Lists the 22 official languages recognised by the Constitution.

 

• Ninth Schedule (Option 2): Added by the First Amendment (1951), it protects listed laws from judicial review on the ground of violation of Fundamental Rights.

 

• Eleventh Schedule (Option 4): Added by the 73rd Amendment (1992), it lists the powers and functions of Panchayati Raj institutions.

question: According to Kautilya's Arthashastra, the Commanding Officer of the cavalry in the Mauryan administration was known as:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ashwadhyaksha.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kautilya's Arthashastra describes a detailed military administration for the Mauryan Empire, with separate superintendents (adhyakshas) for each wing of the army.

 

• The Ashwadhyaksha was the Superintendent/Commanding Officer of the cavalry (ashva = horse), responsible for the training, breeding and maintenance of horses and horsemen. (अश्वाध्यक्ष — घुड़सवार सेना का अध्यक्ष)

 

• The Mauryan army, as described by Megasthenes and the Arthashastra, was organised into six wings under a Senapati, each with its own adhyaksha — infantry, cavalry, chariots, elephants, navy and transport/supply.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Mauryan War Office, per Megasthenes, consisted of a board of thirty members divided into six committees of five members each, one committee for each wing of the armed forces.

 

• The Arthashastra is attributed to Kautilya (Chanakya), chief minister of Chandragupta Maurya, and is a treatise on statecraft, economics and military strategy.

 

NOTE

 

• Rathadhyaksha (Option 1): Superintendent of chariots (ratha), not cavalry.

 

• Hastyadhyaksha (Option 2): Superintendent of elephants (hasti/hasty), the elephant corps.

 

• Patyadhyaksha (Option 4): Superintendent of infantry (pattis/foot soldiers), not cavalry.

question: Doongri festival of Himachal Pradesh is primarily celebrated by which religious community?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Hindu.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Doongri Festival is a Hindu festival celebrated in the Kullu valley of Himachal Pradesh, dedicated to the local deity Goddess Hidimba (Hadimba), the patron goddess of the Kullu region. (डूंगरी उत्सव — हिमाचल प्रदेश, हिडिम्बा देवी)

 

• It is celebrated annually in May, over a period of about three days, near the famous Hadimba Devi Temple in Manali, and includes processions, folk songs, dances and traditional rituals.

 

• The festival reflects the strong local tradition of devi/devta (deity) worship that is characteristic of the folk-Hindu culture of the Kullu-Manali region of Himachal Pradesh.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Hadimba Devi Temple, built in 1553, is a cave-style wooden temple built over a rock considered a symbol of the goddess Hidimba, wife of Bhima from the Mahabharata.

 

• Himachal Pradesh is known for several other local Hindu festivals such as Kullu Dussehra and the Minjar Fair of Chamba.

 

NOTE

 

• Buddhist, Sikh, Muslim (Options 1, 2, 3): The Doongri Festival is not associated with any of these communities; it is a local Hindu deity-worship festival specific to the Kullu valley.

question: Arjun Singh Dhurve was conferred the Padma Shri in 2022 for his contribution to the Baiga dance form of which state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Madhya Pradesh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Arjun Singh Dhurve was awarded the Padma Shri in 2022 in the field of Art for his contribution to preserving the Baiga dance, a traditional dance of the Baiga tribal community of Madhya Pradesh. (बैगा नृत्य — मध्य प्रदेश)

 

• The Baiga tribe is a Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Group (PVTG) found mainly in the Dindori, Mandla, Balaghat and Shahdol districts of Madhya Pradesh, and also in parts of Chhattisgarh.

 

• The Baiga dance is performed on festive and ritual occasions and is closely tied to the tribe's agricultural and forest-based way of life.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Padma Shri is the fourth-highest civilian award in India, conferred by the Government of India for distinguished contribution in various fields including art, social work, and public affairs.

 

• Madhya Pradesh is home to several other prominent tribal dance forms including Gaur Maria and Karma dance.

 

NOTE

 

• Odisha, Rajasthan, West Bengal (Options 1, 2, 3): The Baiga tribe and its dance tradition are not native to these states; Arjun Singh Dhurve's award is specifically linked to Madhya Pradesh.

question: Which of the soluble fibres found in fruits is used as a thickener in cooking and baking?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pectin.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pectin is a soluble dietary fibre naturally found in the cell walls of fruits (especially apples, citrus fruits and guavas) and is widely used as a gelling and thickening agent in cooking and baking, notably in jams and jellies. (पेक्टिन — फलों में पाया जाने वाला घुलनशील रेशा)

 

• Being soluble in water, pectin forms a gel-like consistency when combined with sugar and acid, which is the basis of its use as a thickener.

 

• Soluble fibres like pectin also help slow digestion and are associated with lowering blood cholesterol levels.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other examples of soluble fibre include beta-glucan (in oats and barley) and inulin, while insoluble fibres include cellulose, hemicellulose and lignin.

 

• Dietary fibre is broadly classified into soluble (dissolves in water, forms a gel) and insoluble (does not dissolve, adds bulk to stool) types.

 

NOTE

 

• Lignin (Option 1): An insoluble fibre found in plant cell walls; it is not used as a culinary thickener.

 

• Cellulose (Option 2): An insoluble structural fibre of plant cell walls; it does not dissolve in water and is not used as a thickening agent.

 

• Inulin (Option 4): A soluble fibre, but it is mainly used as a prebiotic and sugar/fat substitute, not primarily as a culinary thickener the way pectin is.

question: 'Vazhuvoor' is one of the styles of which Indian classical dance form?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bharatanatyam.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Vazhuvoor is one of the recognised banis (stylistic schools) of Bharatanatyam, named after the village of Vazhuvoor in Tamil Nadu, and is known for its graceful, sculpturesque and expressive (abhinaya-oriented) movements. (वाझुवूर शैली — भरतनाट्यम)

 

• The Vazhuvoor style was popularised by guru Vazhuvoor Ramaiah Pillai, and is one of the major banis of Bharatanatyam along with the Pandanallur, Thanjavur, Melattur and Kalakshetra styles.

 

• Bharatanatyam originated in Tamil Nadu and is one of the oldest classical dance forms of India, traditionally performed in temples.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Pandanallur bani, developed by Meenakshisundaram Pillai, emphasises linear precision, while the Vazhuvoor bani emphasises fluidity and dramatic expression.

 

• Other Indian classical dance forms and their home states include Kathak (North India), Kathakali and Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Odissi (Odisha), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh) and Manipuri (Manipur).

 

NOTE

 

• Kathak (Option 1): A classical dance of North India, with gharanas such as Jaipur, Lucknow and Banaras — Vazhuvoor is not associated with it.

 

• Kathakali (Option 3): A classical dance-drama of Kerala, distinguished by elaborate costumes and facial makeup.

 

• Mohiniyattam (Option 4): A classical lyrical dance of Kerala, traditionally performed solo by women; Vazhuvoor is not one of its styles.

question: Who was the Mughal emperor during the third battle of Panipat?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Shahalam II.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Third Battle of Panipat was fought on 14 January 1761 between the Maratha Empire and Ahmad Shah Abdali (Durrani), supported by Najib-ud-Daulah and Shuja-ud-Daulah. (शाह आलम द्वितीय — तृतीय पानीपत युद्ध के समय मुगल सम्राट)

 

• Shah Alam II had been proclaimed Mughal emperor in 1759 (formally crowned in 1760) and held the Mughal throne at the time of the battle, although he was away from Delhi campaigning in the east and the imperial capital was effectively controlled by Abdali's allies.

 

• The Marathas suffered a decisive defeat in this battle, which checked their northward expansion and paved the way for the eventual rise of British power in India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The First Battle of Panipat (1526) was fought between Babur and Ibrahim Lodi, establishing Mughal rule; the Second Battle of Panipat (1556) was fought between Akbar's forces (under Bairam Khan) and Hemu.

 

• Shah Alam II later signed the Treaty of Allahabad (1765) with the British East India Company, granting it Diwani rights over Bengal, Bihar and Odisha.

 

NOTE

 

• Akbar II (Option 1): Reigned much later, from 1806 to 1837, and was the father of Bahadur Shah Zafar.

 

• Bahadur Shah I (Option 3): Reigned from 1707 to 1712, decades before the Third Battle of Panipat.

 

• Bahadurshah Jafar (Option 4): The last Mughal emperor (1837-1857), deposed after the Revolt of 1857, long after the Third Battle of Panipat.

question: The Champaran Satyagraha took place in ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1917.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Champaran Satyagraha took place in 1917 in the Champaran district of Bihar, and was Mahatma Gandhi's first Satyagraha movement in India. (चंपारण सत्याग्रह — 1917, बिहार)

 

• It was launched against the exploitative Tinkathia system, under which indigo planters forced peasants to grow indigo on a fixed portion of their land.

 

• Gandhi was invited to Champaran by local peasant leader Raj Kumar Shukla, and the movement led to the setting up of a committee that eventually abolished the Tinkathia system through the Champaran Agrarian Act, 1918.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• After Champaran, Gandhi led the Kheda Satyagraha (1918) in Gujarat over crop failure and tax remission, and the Ahmedabad Mill Strike (1918) over wages.

 

• Gandhi's associates in the Champaran movement included Rajendra Prasad, J.B. Kripalani and Mazharul Haque.

 

NOTE

 

• 1914, 1923, 1920 (Options 1, 2, 4): None of these years mark the Champaran Satyagraha; 1917 is the historically correct year.

question: According to Koeppen's Scheme, which type of climate is denoted by the letter 'E' in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Polar type.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In Koeppen's climate classification scheme, the letter 'E' denotes the Polar type climate, characterised by very low temperatures found in the high-altitude, snow-covered regions of India. (कोपेन जलवायु वर्गीकरण — 'E' प्रकार ध्रुवीय जलवायु)

 

• In India, the 'E' (Polar) type climate is found in the Himalayan region, especially areas at very high altitude with permanent snow/ice cover, such as parts of Jammu & Kashmir, Ladakh and Himachal Pradesh.

 

• Koeppen's scheme uses letters A (Tropical), B (Dry), C (Warm Temperate), D (Cold/Snow) and E (Polar/Ice) as the primary climate group categories, further divided by second and third letters based on precipitation and temperature patterns.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• In India's Koeppen classification, Amw denotes the Monsoon type with short dry winter (Western coast), As denotes Tropical savannah with dry summer, BShw denotes semi-arid steppe, and Dfc/Dfb denote cold humid winter types found in parts of the Himalayas.

 

• The German climatologist Wladimir Koeppen devised this widely used empirical climate classification system in the early 20th century.

 

NOTE

 

• Tropical savannah (Option 1): Denoted by 'A' group with 's' or 'w' subtype (e.g., As, Aw), not 'E'.

 

• Hot desert (Option 2): Falls under the 'B' (Dry) group, denoted as BWhw, not 'E'.

 

• Monsoon with dry summer (Option 3): Denoted by 'A' group (As type), not 'E'.

question: When did Carl Friedrich Gauss and Wilhelm Eduard Weber invent the world's first electromagnetic telegraph?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1833.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• German scientists Carl Friedrich Gauss and Wilhelm Eduard Weber built the world's first electromagnetic telegraph in 1833 at the University of Göttingen, Germany. (विद्युत चुंबकीय टेलीग्राफ — गॉस और वेबर, 1833)

 

• The device connected the observatory and the physics institute in Göttingen over a distance of about 1.2 km, using a galvanometer-based needle system.

 

• This early telegraph predated the more widely commercialised telegraph systems developed later by Samuel Morse (USA) and Cooke and Wheatstone (Britain).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Samuel Morse developed the Morse code and a commercially successful electric telegraph system in the United States, demonstrated publicly in 1837-1844.

 

• The CGS system of units for magnetism owes much to Gauss and Weber's pioneering work; the unit 'gauss' is named after Carl Friedrich Gauss.

 

NOTE

 

• 1832, 1830, 1831 (Options 2, 3, 4): These years are incorrect; the Gauss-Weber telegraph was built and demonstrated in 1833.

question: Who among the following was one of the founders of Rahnumai Mazdayasnan Sabha or Religious Reform Association?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dadabhai Naoroji.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Rahnumai Mazdayasnan Sabha (Religious Reform Association) was founded in 1851 in Bombay to reform Parsi/Zoroastrian religious and social practices along rationalist, modern lines. (रहनुमाई मज़दयस्नान सभा — दादाभाई नौरोजी)

 

• It was founded by a group of Western-educated, progressive Parsis, prominently including Dadabhai Naoroji, along with Naoroji Furdonji, S.S. Bengalee (Bengalee) and Dosabhai Framji Karaka.

 

• The Sabha ran a journal called 'Rast Goftar' ('Truth Teller') to spread its reformist ideas, and worked to remove superstitions and improve the status of women in Parsi society.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Dadabhai Naoroji is also famous as the author of 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India', propounder of the 'Drain of Wealth' theory, and the first Indian to become a British MP (1892).

 

• Parsi reform in the 19th century paralleled other socio-religious reform movements such as the Brahmo Samaj (Bengal) and Prarthana Samaj (Bombay).

 

NOTE

 

• Kesub Chandra Sen (Option 1): A leader of the Brahmo Samaj in Bengal, unrelated to the Parsi reform movement.

 

• Muhammad Iqbal (Option 3): A poet-philosopher associated with the Muslim League/two-nation theory, not the Parsi reform movement.

 

• Aatmarang Pandurang (Atmaram Pandurang) (Option 4): Founder of the Prarthana Samaj (1867) in Bombay, a Hindu reform movement, not the Parsi Rahnumai Mazdayasnan Sabha.

question: In which of the following cities of British India was Lata Mangeshkar born?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Indore.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Legendary playback singer Lata Mangeshkar was born on 28 September 1929 in Indore, then part of the princely state of Indore in British India (Central India Agency). (लता मंगेशकर — इंदौर में जन्म)

 

• She was the eldest child of classical singer and theatre actor Pandit Deenanath Mangeshkar and Shevanti (Shudhamati) Mangeshkar.

 

• Lata Mangeshkar went on to become one of India's most celebrated playback singers, recording songs in numerous Indian languages over a career spanning more than seven decades.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Lata Mangeshkar was honoured with India's highest civilian award, the Bharat Ratna, in 2001, along with the Dadasaheb Phalke Award (1989) and Padma Vibhushan (1999).

 

• She passed away on 6 February 2022 in Mumbai.

 

NOTE

 

• Bombay, Calcutta, Lucknow (Options 1, 2, 3): These were not Lata Mangeshkar's birthplace; she was born in Indore, though she later made Bombay (Mumbai) her career base.

question: When did India first win the first World Cup title in Hockey?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1975.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India won its first (and so far only) Hockey World Cup title in 1975, held in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. (हॉकी विश्व कप — भारत, 1975)

 

• India defeated Pakistan 2-1 in the final, with Ashok Kumar (son of hockey legend Dhyan Chand) scoring the winning goal.

 

• This remains India's only Hockey World Cup title to date, even though India has won multiple Olympic gold medals in hockey.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Men's Hockey World Cup was first held in 1971 in Barcelona, where India won the bronze medal.

 

• India has won 8 Olympic gold medals in hockey, the most recent prior to 2023 being in 1980 (Moscow); India also won Olympic bronze in 2020 Tokyo and 2024 Paris.

 

NOTE

 

• 1978 (Option 2): India did not win the World Cup that year; the title was won by Pakistan.

 

• 1971 (Option 3): This was the first-ever Hockey World Cup, won by Pakistan, with India taking bronze.

 

• 1982 (Option 4): India did not win the World Cup that year; Pakistan won the title, hosted in Mumbai.

question: Which of the following periods is known as the period of population explosion in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1951 - 1981.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In the demographic history of India's population growth, the period 1951-1981 is classified as the phase of 'population explosion', marked by a very high and steadily rising growth rate. (जनसंख्या विस्फोट काल — 1951-1981)

 

• This period saw a sharp decline in the death rate due to improved medical facilities, control of epidemics and famines, and public health measures, while the birth rate remained high, causing rapid population growth.

 

• The Indian census demarcates population growth history broadly into four phases: 1901-1921 (stagnant), 1921-1951 (steady growth), 1951-1981 (population explosion) and 1981 onward (high growth with signs of slowing down).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• 1921 is called the 'Year of the Great Divide' in Indian demography, as it marks the point after which India's population began to grow continuously rather than fluctuating.

 

• Since 1981, India's population growth rate has gradually decelerated due to the impact of family planning programmes and rising literacy, though the absolute population continues to grow.

 

NOTE

 

• 1981-2021 (Option 1): This is the phase of high growth with a declining growth rate, not the explosion phase.

 

• 1931-1961 (Option 2): Not the standard demarcated period; it overlaps two different phases (steady growth and explosion).

 

• 1921-1951 (Option 3): This is classified as the phase of 'steady growth', preceding the population explosion phase.

question: Which of the following is NOT one of the scenarios of National Digital Education Architecture (NDEAR) launched by the Government of India in 2021?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Develop Learn.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The National Digital Education Architecture (NDEAR) was launched by the Ministry of Education, Government of India, in 2021 to provide a unifying digital infrastructure for education across states and platforms. (राष्ट्रीय डिजिटल शिक्षा वास्तुकला — NDEAR, 2021)

 

• NDEAR is designed around three core usage scenarios: 'Learn' (access to learning content and resources), 'Manage Learn' (management of learning activities, courses and assessments for educators/administrators), and 'Help Learn' (support to learners through mentoring, chatbots and grievance redressal).

 

• 'Develop Learn' is not one of the defined NDEAR scenarios — it does not appear in NDEAR's official documentation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• NDEAR builds on principles similar to India Stack/DEPA, providing federated, interoperable and modular digital building blocks for states to build their own education platforms.

 

• NDEAR supports initiatives such as DIKSHA (Digital Infrastructure for Knowledge Sharing), a national platform for school education content.

 

NOTE

 

• Manage Learn (Option 1): A genuine NDEAR scenario covering management of learning processes.

 

• Learn (Option 2): A genuine NDEAR scenario covering access to learning content.

 

• Help Learn (Option 4): A genuine NDEAR scenario covering learner support services.

question: Which form of leucoplast specialises in oil synthesis and storage and is mainly found in the layer of cells in pollen grains that develop pollen grains?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Elaioplasts.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Elaioplasts are a form of leucoplast (colourless plastid) that specialise in the synthesis and storage of oils/lipids, and are commonly found in the tapetum layer of cells that nourish and develop pollen grains within the anther. (एलियोप्लास्ट — तेल संश्लेषण एवं भंडारण करने वाला ल्यूकोप्लास्ट)

 

• Leucoplasts are non-pigmented plastids found in non-photosynthetic parts of plants (roots, seeds, tubers), and are classified based on the substance they store: amyloplasts (starch), proteinoplasts (protein) and elaioplasts (oil/fat).

 

• The oils stored by elaioplasts are important for pollen coat formation, pollen viability and pollen-stigma recognition during fertilisation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Plastids are broadly classified into chloroplasts (photosynthetic, green), chromoplasts (pigmented, e.g. in flowers/fruits) and leucoplasts (colourless, storage).

 

• Amyloplasts, the starch-storing leucoplasts, are the most abundant type and are found in storage organs such as potato tubers.

 

NOTE

 

• Gerontoplasts (Option 1): These are plastids formed from the degeneration of chloroplasts during leaf senescence (ageing), not oil storage.

 

• Proteinoplasts (Option 2): A type of leucoplast that stores proteins, not oils.

 

• Chloroplasts (Option 3): These are photosynthetic, pigmented plastids containing chlorophyll, not colourless leucoplasts, and are not the plastid type described.

question:
Which of the following statements are correct regarding the State Executive?

A. Article 152 of the Indian Constitution states 'Unless the context otherwise requires, the expression 'State' does not include Jammu and Kashmir'.

B. The 7th Constitutional Amendment Act has provided for the appointment of the same person as Governor for two or more states.

C. The Supreme Court clearly mentioned that the office of the Governor is under the control of the Central Government.
solution_text:
The correct answer is A and B only.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement A is correct: Article 152 of the Constitution defines the expression 'State' for Part VI, and (as originally enacted) explicitly excludes the State of Jammu and Kashmir from this definition. (अनुच्छेद 152 और 153 — राज्यपाल संबंधी प्रावधान)

 

• Statement B is correct: The 7th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1956 amended Article 153 to permit the appointment of the same person as Governor for two or more States, allowing common governors — a provision still used today.

 

• Statement C is incorrect: The Supreme Court has consistently held that the Governor is NOT under the control of, or subordinate to, the Central Government in the exercise of his constitutional discretionary functions; the Governor is an independent constitutional authority, not an agent of the Union.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 153 originally provided for one Governor per state; the 7th Amendment Act, 1956 (also responsible for the reorganisation of states on a linguistic basis) inserted the provision for common governors.

 

• The Governor is appointed by the President and holds office 'during the pleasure of the President' (Article 156), but exercises many functions on the aid and advice of the State Council of Ministers, and discretionary functions independently — not under Central Government control.

 

NOTE

 

• B and C only (Option 1): Incorrect because it wrongly includes C and excludes A, which is a correct statement.

 

• A and C only (Option 2): Incorrect because it wrongly includes C, which is factually incorrect.

 

• A, B and C (Option 3): Incorrect because it wrongly includes C alongside the two correct statements A and B.

question: The 'East-West' corridor connects which of the following cities?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Silchar and Porbandar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The East-West Corridor, developed under the National Highways Development Project (NHDP) Phase II, connects Silchar in Assam to Porbandar in Gujarat, spanning about 3,300 km. (पूर्व-पश्चिम गलियारा — सिलचर से पोरबंदर)

 

• It passes through the states of Assam, West Bengal, Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan and Gujarat.

 

• The East-West Corridor intersects the North-South Corridor (connecting Srinagar to Kanyakumari) near Jhansi, together forming a major highway grid across India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The North-South Corridor connects Srinagar (J&K) to Kanyakumari (Tamil Nadu), with a link to Kochi, covering about 4,000 km.

 

• The North-South and East-West Corridors, along with the Golden Quadrilateral, together constitute the NHDP's core highway network aimed at improving connectivity across India.

 

NOTE

 

• Itanagar and Dwarka, Guwahati and Gandhinagar, Shillong and Kandla (Options 1, 2, 3): None of these city pairs represent the officially designated East-West Corridor, which specifically runs between Silchar and Porbandar.

question: The centre of a cyclone is a calm area. It is called the ______ of the storm.
solution_text:
The correct answer is eye.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The calm, clear area at the centre of a cyclone is called the 'eye' of the storm. (चक्रवात की आंख)

 

• The eye is typically 30-65 km in diameter, characterised by light winds, clear or partly cloudy skies and relatively low pressure at the very centre, in stark contrast to the violently rotating winds surrounding it.

 

• Surrounding the eye is the 'eyewall', a ring of towering thunderstorm clouds where the most severe winds and heaviest rainfall of the cyclone occur.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Cyclones are known by different regional names: 'hurricanes' in the Atlantic/Northeast Pacific, 'typhoons' in the Northwest Pacific, and 'cyclones' in the South Pacific and Indian Ocean.

 

• Tropical cyclones form over warm ocean waters (usually above 26.5°C) and derive their energy from the latent heat released by condensation of water vapour.

 

NOTE

 

• Base, focal point, trigger point (Options 1, 2, 4): These are not the meteorological terms used for the calm centre of a cyclone; the correct term is specifically the 'eye'.

question: The feature of fundamental duties in the Indian Constitution is adopted from which of the following countries?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Soviet Union (USSR).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The concept of Fundamental Duties in the Indian Constitution (Part IV-A, Article 51A) was borrowed from the erstwhile Soviet Union (USSR). (मौलिक कर्तव्य — सोवियत संघ (USSR) से प्रेरित)

 

• Fundamental Duties were not part of the original Constitution (1950); they were added later by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976, on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee, initially listing 10 duties (a 11th was added by the 86th Amendment, 2002).

 

• Unlike Fundamental Rights, Fundamental Duties are not legally enforceable by courts, but serve as a constant reminder to citizens of their moral obligations towards the nation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Several other constitutional features are also borrowed from various countries: Fundamental Rights and Judicial Review from the USA, the Parliamentary system and Rule of Law from the UK, and Directive Principles of State Policy from Ireland.

 

• The 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002 added a 11th Fundamental Duty, making it a duty of parents/guardians to provide education to children aged 6-14 years.

 

NOTE

 

• UK (Option 1): The UK is the source of India's parliamentary system, rule of law and single citizenship, not Fundamental Duties.

 

• Germany (Option 2): Germany is the source of the provision for 'Suspension of Fundamental Rights during Emergency', not Fundamental Duties.

 

• US (Option 3): The US is the source of India's Fundamental Rights, Judicial Review, Independence of Judiciary and the concept of a written Constitution, not Fundamental Duties.

question: The Nehru trophy boat race was organised by which of the following states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kerala.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Nehru Trophy Boat Race is organised annually in Kerala, held on the Punnamada Lake at Alappuzha (Alleppey), typically on the second Saturday of August. (नेहरू ट्रॉफी वल्लमकली — केरल)

 

• It features the traditional 'Chundan Vallam' (snake boats) of Kerala, and is one of the most popular boat races and cultural spectacles associated with Kerala's backwaters.

 

• The race gets its name from Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru, India's first Prime Minister, who was so impressed by a boat race welcome given to him in 1952 that he donated a trophy, which has since been awarded to the winning team every year.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kerala's backwaters and boat race tradition are closely tied to its identity as 'God's Own Country', and the Nehru Trophy Boat Race is a major tourist attraction.

 

• Other notable snake boat races in Kerala include the Champakulam Moolam Boat Race and the Aranmula Boat Race.

 

NOTE

 

• Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, West Bengal (Options 1, 2, 3): The Nehru Trophy Boat Race is not organised in any of these states; it is specific to Alappuzha, Kerala.

question: As mentioned in the Government of India's Economic Survey 2022-23, Aadhaar is an essential tool for social delivery of how many Central Schemes as notified under Section 7 of the Aadhaar Act, 2016?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 318.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• According to the Economic Survey 2022-23, Aadhaar has become an essential tool for the social delivery of 318 Central Schemes as notified under Section 7 of the Aadhaar (Targeted Delivery of Financial and Other Subsidies, Benefits and Services) Act, 2016. (आधार — आर्थिक सर्वेक्षण 2022-23, 318 केंद्रीय योजनाएं)

 

• Section 7 of the Aadhaar Act allows the Central/State Government to require Aadhaar authentication as a condition for receipt of a subsidy, benefit or service, where expenditure is from the Consolidated Fund of India.

 

• The Economic Survey highlighted Aadhaar-linked Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) as central to improving targeting and reducing leakages in government welfare schemes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Major Aadhaar-linked schemes notified under Section 7 include the Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana, PM-KISAN, MGNREGA and the Public Distribution System (PDS).

 

• The Economic Survey is presented in Parliament a day before the Union Budget and is prepared under the guidance of the Chief Economic Adviser.

 

NOTE

 

• 228, 564, 720 (Options 1, 2, 4): These figures are incorrect; the Economic Survey 2022-23 specifically cites 318 Central Schemes notified under Section 7.

question: Which suffix is used when the –CHO group is attached to a carbon atom of a ring or ring system, or to a heteroatom?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Carbaldehyde.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per IUPAC nomenclature, when the -CHO (aldehyde) group is attached to a carbon atom that is part of a ring or ring system, the compound is named using the suffix '-carbaldehyde', since the carbon of -CHO is not counted as part of the ring's own carbon skeleton. (कार्बाल्डिहाइड — वलय से जुड़े -CHO समूह हेतु प्रत्यय)

 

• For example, an aldehyde group attached to a cyclohexane ring is named cyclohexanecarbaldehyde, and one attached to benzene is named benzenecarbaldehyde (benzaldehyde being its common/retained name).

 

• This is distinct from a chain aldehyde, where the -CHO carbon is counted in the main chain and the suffix '-al' is used instead (e.g. ethanal, propanal).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• For chain compounds, aldehydes take the suffix '-al' (e.g., methanal, ethanal); for dialdehydes, the suffix '-dial' is used.

 

• IUPAC nomenclature uses similar 'ring-attachment' suffixes for other functional groups too, such as '-carboxylic acid' for a -COOH group attached to a ring.

 

NOTE

 

• Amide (Option 1): The suffix used for the functional group -CONH2, not for -CHO attached to a ring.

 

• Halide (Option 2): Refers to compounds containing a halogen atom (-X), unrelated to the aldehyde (-CHO) functional group.

 

• Nitrile (Option 3): The suffix '-carbonitrile'/'-nitrile' is used for the -C≡N (cyano) functional group, not -CHO.
